narrative.overview:
Measured Momentum is a dark theatrical sports editorial built from photographic emulsion, contact-sheet registration, and visible evidence. The shipped system turns the energy of Acrobatic Rock ’n’ Roll and Boogie Woogie into a persuasive sequence without presenting the proposal as an operating federation or programme. It records the finished transformation from concept seed `d8310e56`; the built artifact, including its final homepage review image, is the authority.

The world is premium because it is controlled rather than glossy. Warm-ivory type sits on near-black stages; supplied rehearsal photography arrives as full-bleed or deliberately offset plates; lime, pink, teal, indigo, and brass behave like registration inks, count marks, and evidence signals. Fine rules, crop marks, eight-count rails, and source-like captions provide structure. Controls are solid typographic objects. Essential meaning remains static and readable while Saath Rekha contributes only deferred, nonessential depth.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black photographic emulsion with warm-ivory type.
Lime, pink, and teal registration marks, with indigo links and brass evidence cues.
Twelve-column editorial fields and recurring eight-count measurement rails.
Full-bleed or offset supplied performance plates with provenance captions.
Static-first meaning with deferred, decorative Saath Rekha depth.

rules.name: The Registration Ink Rule
rules.body: Bright colors appear as status fields, type accents, count marks, crop marks, rules, and bounded action slabs; they are not ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Truthful Status Rule
rules.body: Registration Lime may make the proposal status impossible to miss, but color never replaces the exact “Proposed organisation · In development” wording.

rules.name: The Accessible Pairing Rule
rules.body: State, validation, discipline, and selection always retain a textual, structural, or shape cue in addition to color.

rules.name: The Condensed Arena Rule
rules.body: Use Barlow Condensed for headlines and emphatic numerals, not for long-form body copy.

rules.name: The Metadata Is Evidence Rule
rules.body: Monospaced uppercase text is reserved for real status, count, navigation, measurement, and source information; never use it to invent an ornamental kicker.

rules.name: The Measured Field Rule
rules.body: Align persuasive surfaces to twelve columns and rhythmic metadata to eight counts; asymmetry is deliberate, but edges always register.

rules.name: The Photograph Is a Plate Rule
rules.body: Performance imagery is full-bleed or staggered and receives a source caption; it is never presented as an anonymous generic card gallery.

rules.name: The Plate, Not Card Rule
rules.body: Use overlap, crop, contrast, and one purposeful shadow to establish depth; do not wrap every idea in a glowing elevated card.

rules.name: The Fallback First Rule
rules.body: The photograph, HTML, and CSS composition must be complete before Saath Rekha loads; removing WebGL cannot remove meaning.

rules.name: The Registration Edge Rule
rules.body: Default to a square edge; round only when the shape expresses focus, orbit, partnership, or a native control affordance.

dos: Do keep “Proposed organisation · In development” visibly present in the global shell and pair visual status with exact explanatory language.
Do use self-hosted Barlow Condensed for high-impact display roles and system fonts for readable editorial copy.
Do treat supplied performance images as illustrative plates with truthful provenance and non-claim captions.
Do use lime, pink, teal, indigo, and brass as measured registration inks, preserving Strong or Body Ivory for sustained reading.
Do keep essential information in semantic HTML and preserve static, reduced-motion, forced-colors, print, and no-WebGL fallbacks.
Do keep editorial routes static-export compatible, trailing-slashed, and independent of request-time page data.
donts: Don't imply legal status, recognition, affiliation, authority, people, results, events, sponsors, official contact details, or operating services without verified evidence and publication approval.
Don't turn the world into a generic dark sports landing page made from a centered slogan, decorative glass cards, anonymous statistics, or repeated ambient glows.
Don't use invented kickers, glyph icons, or monospaced labels as empty decoration; every metadata treatment must carry real status, count, navigation, measurement, or source information.
Don't make Saath Rekha essential, immediate, motion-dependent, or more visually authoritative than the proposal and its evidence.
Don't return visual or copy success for an enquiry unless durable, server-validated persistence and its controls are configured and verified.
